newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rail strike in southeastern France resolved.
newsitem.headline: Rail strike in southeastern France resolved.

text.p: A rail strike that had disrupted train service in southeastern France for six days ended on Saturday after the SNCF national rail authority agreed to keep jobs it had wanted to eliminate, SNCF officials said.
"Management has agreed after negotiations to preserve all of the jobs in the Marseille depot," an official said.
The strike had disrupted regional train service and some longer routes but had not affected TGV high-speed trains or lines serving Riviera cities along the Mediterranean coast.
Negotiations between union representatives and SNCF managers had begun on Friday and resumed on Saturday afternoon.

The two most powerful SNCF unions had earlier asked members to join a nationwide strike called for October 17 by civil service unions seeking pay raises and protesting against the centre- right government's plans to do away with 6,000 public jobs next year.
Railworkers led a crippling 24-day public sector strike late last year when Prime Minister Alain Juppe proposed ending early pension rights -- plans which have since been scrapped.

The concern this time is over programmed job cuts and a modernisation plan under which the government will take 125 billion francs ($25 billion) of debt off the loss-making SNCF by spinning it off into another state company which would also become owner of the track and other infrastructure.
Unions fear the plan could open the way to additional staff cuts or a possible privatisation of the SNCF.
